headline: Agreed to begin a tree inventory on Swarthmore Street; approved previous meeting minutes as amended.
summary: Members discussed pin oak trees on Swarthmore Street and agreed to start a focused tree inventory there. They also discussed tree-safety emails, the Trees for Communities grant, and a planned volunteer workday. Members approved the prior minutes as amended.
decisions: Approved the August 18, 2026 meeting minutes as amended.
Agreed that Swarthmore Street will be the starting location for a focused tree inventory that documents number, species, size, and location of trees.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Tree Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
5:30 PM, September 15, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2nd Floor Conference 
Room 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER   
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner Dr. M. Montgomery at 5:32 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE   
 The Clerk called the roll, and the following members were present: 
Commissioner Dr. Michael Montgomery, Chair 
Commissioner Susan L. Neitlich 
Commissioner Diane E. Hoffman 
Commissioner Dr. Nathan Havill 
Commissioner Kyle Dougherty 
 
Also in attendance were Christopher Rhone, Tree Warden; Joseph Colello, Director of 
Public Works; and Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk. 
 
Roll Call Summary: Present, Voting: 5; Present, Not Voting: 0; Absent: 0; Excused: 0. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 
 
  1. Regular Meeting of August 18, 2026   
  The Commission reviewed the minutes of the August 18, 2026 Regular Meeting. 
 
Chair Dr. M. Montgomery discussed the supplemental materials included with the 
meeting materials, including photographs, correspondence, and links to videos 
submitted by residents. He noted that this method made supporting information the 
Commission received available to commissioners and the public. 
 
The following corrections were identified: 
 
• “New Haven Alliance for Trees” was corrected to “Hamden Alliance for Trees” 
in the Friends of the Library Audio-Podcast: Participation subsection under Old 
Business. 
“…all residents of Swathmore Street.” was corrected to “…all residents of 
Swarthmore Street.” in the Attendance section.
A motion was made and seconded to approve the August 18, 2026 meeting minutes 
as amended. The motion passed. 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 There were no members of the public present in person or participating virtually. No public 
comments were received. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE   
 Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that the Commission had received a significant 
amount of correspondence since the previous meeting, including three tree requests and 
approximately nine emails concerning tree safety issues. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery noted that several of the tree-safety emails had been sent to 
the Commission without copying the Tree Warden. He forwarded those matters to the Tree 
Warden and expressed concern that residents may not have a clear understanding of how 
to report tree-related safety issues directly to the appropriate Town department. The 
Commission brought the issue to Town officials for review. 
 
The Commission also received correspondence from a resident who wished to withdraw 
from the Trees for Communities program. Chair Dr. M. Montgomery discussed the 
importance of being sensitive to residents' individual circumstances when following up on 
tree requests. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty reported that he had contacted Gail Cameron regarding a 
potential tree-related presentation for the Hamden Land Conservation Trust. A Saturday in 
October was being considered, with October 17 or October 24 discussed as possible 
dates. Commissioner Dougherty will follow up regarding scheduling. 
 
  
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No Executive Session was held. 
7. REPORTS   
 
 
  1. Tree Warden Report  
  Tree Warden Christopher Rhone reported that United Illuminating's recent circuit work 
was substantially complete. 
 
Tree Warden C. Rhone reported that he met with a Lewis Tree representative about 
proposed capital tree work between Hamden High School and the adjacent shopping 
plaza. The area contains a significant number of Tree-of-Heaven ('Ailanthus 
altissima') trees near electrical infrastructure. The trees appear to be primarily on 
private property, and the utility will need to coordinate with the property owner. Any 
work involving town trees will require appropriate authorization. 
 
Tree Warden C. Rhone also reported on several recent tree removals and pruning
activities throughout Town, including the removal of declining or dead sugar maples 
and other hazardous trees. He discussed several service requests involving dead 
limbs, storm damage, branches affecting utility service lines, and branches extending 
toward residences. 
 
The Commission discussed a large oak requiring additional inspection due to a 
substantially hollow leader. Tree Warden C. Rhone stated that the hazardous leader 
would be addressed and that the remainder of the tree would be inspected to 
determine whether additional action is necessary. 
 
The Commission discussed the need for additional arboricultural assistance. 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that he had begun compiling a list of 
Connecticut-licensed arborists in Hamden and surrounding communities. 
Commissioner S. Hoffman agreed to continue compiling the list. The Commission 
discussed using the list to help identify potential candidates for the Town's consulting 
arborist position. 
 
Mr. Rhone was thanked for removing a Tree-of-Heaven from a tree grate. 
Commissioners noted the association between Tree-of-Heaven and spotted 
lanternflies. 
 
  
8. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  1. Friends of the Library Audio-Podcast  
  The Commission reported that the Friends of the Library audio podcast had been 
posted to the Hamden Public Library website. The podcast includes information 
concerning trees and related topics. 
 
A link to the completed podcast will be provided to the Clerk for inclusion with the 
meeting materials/minutes. 
 
Please see the link to the podcast below: 
Hamden Public Library Podcast — BONUS EPISODE: Forest Bathing and The 
Hamden Canopy 
  2. Whitneyville Library Shrub and Tree Renovation  
  Commissioner S. Neitlich reported that the next volunteer workday at the Whitneyville 
Branch Library was scheduled for Sunday, September 20, 2026, from 9:30 am to 
12:00 pm. 
 
About ten volunteers helped plan the project. A smaller planning group developed the 
garden design and selected plants, with support from individuals with native plant and 
Master Gardener experience. 
 
The Friends of the Library provided funding for the project. The Commission 
purchased native plants from Earth Tones Native Plant Nursery. The Commission 
discussed obtaining mulch and compost needed to complete the planting area.
The project will include a variety of native plantings. The Commission also plans to 
plant a redbud tree as part of subsequent tree-planting work. 
  3. Trees for Communities Grant (Webpage, Fall Plans)  
  The Commission discussed the Trees for Communities Grant webpage and public 
outreach materials. Commissioners emphasized that residents should be able to 
easily find information describing the program and the tree request form online, 
especially since the webpage will be referenced in outreach materials and door 
hangers. 
 
The Commission discussed plans for fall planting and the current list of requested 
trees. Chair Dr. M. Montgomery reported that the planting list had been developed 
through canvassing, resident requests, and site review. 
 
The Commission discussed anticipated fall planting events, volunteer participation, 
tree delivery, equipment, watering responsibilities, and coordination with Public 
Works. The Commission also discussed the possibility of spring planting for certain 
locations and species where spring conditions may be more appropriate. 
 
The Commission discussed purchasing equipment through grant funding to help 
move balled-and-burlapped trees. 
 
Chair Dr. M. Montgomery also discussed compliance requirements associated with 
the grant and the need to maintain appropriate documentation for expenditures and 
activities. 
  4. Tree Inventory  
  Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery presented information concerning the Town's tree 
inventory and discussed the Commission's responsibility to help develop and maintain 
an inventory of public trees. 
 
The Commission noted that the Town already has an inventory system containing tree 
information and that various records document approximately 600 trees planted since 
2015. The Trees for Communities Grant also requires the GPS coordinates and 
health of grant-funded trees to be documented and monitored. 
 
The Commission discussed working with Town staff to better understand the existing 
inventory system and determine how commissioners and volunteers could help collect 
and enter tree information. 
 
Chair Dr. M. Montgomery stated that commissioners and volunteers could collect tree 
identification, location, species, diameter, and other objective information, while 
qualified arborists should assess tree health and risk. 
 
The Commission expressed interest in recruiting additional volunteers to assist with 
the inventory project. 
9. NEW BUSINESS   
 
 
  1. Swarthmore Street Pin Oak Trees
The Commission discussed the mature pin oak trees located along Swarthmore 
Street and recent tree failures in the area. 
 
The Commission discussed the trees' age and size, limited growing space, sidewalk 
and curb conditions, soil saturation, and how these conditions may affect the trees' 
root systems. 
 
The Commission agreed that Swarthmore Street would be an appropriate location to 
begin a focused inventory effort. The initial work would document the number, 
species, size, and location of trees rather than attempt to assess tree health. 
 
Tree Warden C. Rhone stated that he intends to have an arborist conduct a risk 
assessment of the trees. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery proposed coordinating with Town staff regarding the 
existing inventory system and then organizing commissioners and volunteers to 
conduct field inventory work on Swarthmore Street. 
 
The Commission discussed similar issues involving mature pin oaks in other areas of 
Town but agreed that Swarthmore Street would serve as the initial focus. 
  2. Approval of 2027 Meeting Calendar  
  The Commission discussed the requirement to approve its 2027 meeting calendar. 
 
The Commission clarified that the calendar the Clerk previously distributed was its 
existing 2026 meeting schedule, not a proposed 2027 schedule. 
 
The Clerk recommended that the Commission review and approve the 2027 calendar 
at its October meeting so that it can be completed before the applicable November 
deadline. 
 
The Commission also discussed reserving the 2nd Floor Conference Room for its 
remaining 2026 meetings. It was reported that the September meeting had not 
appeared on the internal room schedule despite the Commission's established 
meeting schedule. 
 
The Clerk agreed to follow up with the Town Clerk's Office to confirm that the 2nd 
Floor Conference Room is reserved for the Tree Commission on the third Tuesday of 
each month at 5:30 PM for the remainder of the year. Chair Montgomery also agreed 
to follow up with the Mayor's Office regarding the room scheduling process. 
10. ANNOUCEMENTS   
 The Commission discussed its participation in the Brooksvale Fall Festival on September 
26, 2026, from 11:00 am to 4:00 pm. 
 
The Tree Commission will have a table at the event. Commissioner K. Dougherty will lead 
the Commission's participation, with the Trees for Communities program as a primary 
outreach focus. 
11. ADJOURNMENT
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery requested a motion to adjourn the meeting. 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
 
The meeting adjourned at approximately 7:25 pm.
